The '''Alliance''', also known as the '''Grand Alliance''', is one of two major political factions of the mortal races in [[Azeroth]], its counterpart being the [[Horde]]. Driven by tradition, the Alliance consists of powerful cultures and groups bound not by desperation or necessity, but by their deep commitments to abstract concepts like nobility, honor, faith, justice, and sacrifice. Striving to represent these high ideals, its many different peoples all contribute their technical, arcane, and spiritual wisdom toward the shared goal of preserving order on Azeroth and creating a peaceful and just world. The Grand Alliance can be considered an evolution of the [[Alliance of Lordaeron]], the memories of the allegiances and idealism of the Alliance of Lordaeron ― centered in the homonymous continent ― served as the ultimate inspiration for the new Alliance of the present day. The modern organization has the bulk of its forces on Northern Kalimdor and the south-eastern continents of [[Khaz Modan]] and [[Azeroth]]. Some of the members of the previous Alliance (such as [[Stormwind]] and [[Ironforge]]) are members of the Grand Alliance. == Background == With [[Lordaeron]]'s fall and the devastation of the northern kingdoms, the rebuilt city of [[Stormwind]] became the new base of the Alliance, with the [[Bronzebeard dwarf|Bronzebeard dwarves]] becoming their staunchest and closest geographical allies. The [[Gnome|gnomes]] of [[Gnomeregan (nation)|Gnomeregan]] had been unable to help in the Third War as they were dealing with their own issues closer to home — namely a [[trogg]] invasion of their city. Because an invasion of troggs paled in comparison to the might of the Scourge, the gnomes decided they would fight their war alone. In the end, following [[Sicco Thermaplugg]]'s treachery, they were forced to flee [[Gnomeregan]] and with their High Tinker, [[Gelbin Mekkatorque]], settled in [[Ironforge]] with the dwarves as refugees. Indebted to their allies for their hospitality in their time of need, the gnomes again offered their services to the Alliance. The night elves, dealing with the loss of their immortality and having been exposed to the world outside their forests once more, decided they would have to make alliances with the wider world. Because of the animosity with the orcs for their continuing lumbering of [[Warsong Gulch]], the night elves, in the end, joined the Alliance. Five years later, the High Elves of Quel'thalas began to gather in caravans and travel south after the abandonment and apparent betrayal of Kael'thalas Sunstrider, seeing that her people needed her, Vereesa joined the Silvermoon Remnant, and began acting as Speaker of this faction, eventually getting her people to reunify with the Alliance once again. == Alliance Member Races == The Alliance is made up of five noble races. === {{RaceIcon|Human|Male}} {{RaceIcon|Human|Female}} [[Humans]]: === One of the founding races and the youngest of the 5 races that make up the Alliance, diplomatic and full of life, they are the main pillar of the Alliance and those who keep it together in addition to being the largest race in terms of population. Its greatest stronghold is Stormwind City after the fall of the Kingdom of Lordaeron in the Third War. Its main leader is [[Anduin Wrynn]], the King of [[Stormwind]]. === {{RaceIcon|Dwarf|Male}} {{RaceIcon|Dwarf|Female}} [[Dwarves]]: === The Dwarves of Khaz Modan and the Wildhammer, known for their robust forge and very powerful war machinery, in addition to being one of the oldest in Azeroth. Their capital, Ironforge, hidden among the mountains of Dun Morogh, stands as the largest dwarven stronghold after the War of the Three Hammers, their brothers, the Wildhammer Dwarves, are located in the mountains of The Hinterlands. Proud and with a strong relationship with the human race, they did not hesitate to join the New Alliance after the fall of the Kingdom of Lordaeron and the disintegration of the [[Alliance of Lordaeron]], they feel that they have a life debt that they will never be able to repay to humans. Its main leader is [[Magni Bronzebeard]], Lord of [[Ironforge]] and the King of [[Khaz Modan]]. === {{RaceIcon|Gnome|Male}} {{RaceIcon|Gnome|Female}} [[Gnomes]]: === The ingenious gnomes of Gnomeregan, of short stature but great intellect, have maintained a strong relationship with the dwarves of Ironforge and this has led them to join the Great Alliance, although they did not participate in the Third War due to their problems with Troggs in their city, have rejoined the Alliance after the betrayal of Sicco Thermoplug. Thus, they lend their ingenuity and inventions as they fight alongside the Alliance to recover their lost capital. Its main leader is [[Gelbin Mekkatorque]], the King of Gnomes and the High Tinker of [[Gnomeregan]]. === {{RaceIcon|NightElf|Male}} {{RaceIcon|NightElf|Female}} [[Night Elves]]: === The mysterious and secretive Night Elves had maintained cordial relations with both the Alliance and the Horde after the third war, with the loss of their beloved World Tree, they had decided to go out into the world once again. But the constant aggressions of the Horde towards their forests and their people, pushed them to formally join the Alliance and sever any relationship with the Horde, thus, as members of the Alliance, they lend their vast ancient knowledge to their new allies as they fight for Defend your forests from the Wild Horde. Its main leader is [[Tyrande Whisperwind]], The High Priestess of [[Elune]], and, in absence of [[Malfurion Stormrage]], [[Fandral Staghelm]]. === {{RaceIcon|HighElf|Male}} {{RaceIcon|HighElf|Female}} [[High elf|High Elves]]: === The proud and magical High Elves of Quel'thalas suffered great losses during the Third War, when the plague swept through Quel'thalas, destroying Silvermoon and the Sunwell, and killing the majority of the elven population. reducing it to historical limits. Repentant, the Elves have migrated south in search of a new future, with the help of Vereesa Windrunner, they were accepted back into the Alliance while struggling with their political problems and addiction to arcane magic. Its main leader is [[Astalor Sunsworn]], after being named Lord Regent of [[Quel'thalas]] by the [[Regency Council]]. [[Category:Organizations]] [[Category:Factions]]

'''Human Alliance''',''Warcraft II: The Dark Saga'' manual, [https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_The_Dark_Saga_manual#The_Human_Alliance The Human Alliance] or '''old Alliance'''[[Colonel Hardinus#On-click]]) was the union of the [[Seven Kingdoms|seven human kingdoms]], along with the [[Dwarf|dwarves]] of [[Khaz Modan]] (which also included the [[Gnome|gnomes]] of [[Gnomeregan (nation)|Gnomeregan]]) and [[Aerie Peak]], the [[High elf|high elves]] of [[Quel'Thalas (kingdom)|Quel'Thalas]], and others with major political influence including the [[Church of Light]]. This coalition formed as a response to the threat of the [[Old Horde|Orcish Horde]] during the [[Second War]]. ==History== ===Second War=== Following the destruction of the [[Stormwind (kingdom)|Kingdom of Azeroth]] by the [[Orcish Horde]] during the [[First War]], its survivors fled to [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]]. Realizing the threat the [[orc]]s posed, [[Anduin Lothar|Regent Lord Anduin Lothar]], leader of Azeroth's refugees, was able to convince the leaders of the other human kingdoms to unify against the orcs as the Alliance. The [[Wildhammer clan|Wildhammer]] dwarves of [[Aerie Peak]] and high elves also soon joined the Alliance, as well as the gnomes of Gnomeregan and the [[Ironforge (kingdom)|Ironforge]] dwarves later in the war. The Church of Light was a strong supporter of Alliance's effort. During the First War, the Clerics of Northshire bravely supported the armies of the kingdom of Stormwind with clerics who healed wounds and channeled devastating powers of Holy Light against their foes. Following the destruction of Stormwind, Archbishop Alonsus Faol was one of the key figures in forming of the Alliance. Having perceived that the pious Clerics of Northshire, who suffered such terrible attrition in the First War, were ill-suited for the dangers of combat, he, along with many of the surviving Clerics of Northshire, sought those of only the greatest virtue among the knighthood of Lordaeron and tutored them in the ways of magic. Christening them the Knights of the Silver Hand, it now rested upon the newly-formed paladins to heal the wounds sustained in combat and to restore faith in the promise of freedom from Orcish tyranny.''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#Alliance_Ground_Units Alliance Ground Units]'', Paladin The Alliance — under the leadership of Sir Anduin Lothar as its Supreme Allied Commander — ultimately defeated the [[Old Horde]] during the battle of [[Blackrock Spire]]. Although Anduin Lothar was slain by [[Warchief]] [[Orgrim Doomhammer]], his death inspired [[Turalyon]] to push the Alliance to victory. Turalyon's forces succeeded in destroying the [[Dark Portal]], the mystical gateway that connected the orcs to their homeworld of [[Draenor]]. Cut off from its reinforcements and fractured by infighting, the Horde finally buckled in upon itself and fell before the might of the Alliance, thus ending the [[Second War]]. The scattered orc clans were quickly rounded up and placed within guarded internment camps under the [[Alliance Internment Act]]. Though it seemed that the Horde had been defeated for good, some remained highly skeptical that peace would last. [[Khadgar]], now an [[Archmage]] of some renown, convinced the Alliance [[High Command|high command]] to build the fortress of [[Nethergarde Keep]] that would watch over the ruins of the Dark Portal and ensure that there would be no further invasions from Draenor.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Alliance_of_Lordaeron The Alliance of Lordaeron] After the death of Lothar, the Alliance of Lordaeron was led by King [[Terenas Menethil II]]. He accepted ambassadors or the monarchs from all member nations and races to his capital. Rarely did the monarchs of the major realms come together. Generally, they spoke through couriers and diplomats, with the occasional state visit thrown in as well.''Day of the Dragon'', pg. 79 One of the inner council of the Kirin Tor had ever been present at such events (with the exception of one meeting Dalaran was not invited, led by Lord [[Deathwing|Daval Prestor]], though spied upon by [[Krasus]]).''Day of the Dragon'', pg. 86 - 87 ===Political crises=== Several nations left the Alliance in response to decisions made after the Second War, including King Terenas's institution of a tax to fund the orcish internment camps and fund the rebuilding of Stormwind.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Alliance_Splinters The Alliance Splinters] Furthermore, there have been [[Alterac crisis|heated debates]] on what to do with the vacant territories of the treasonous [[Alterac (kingdom)|Kingdom of Alterac]], with the [[Stromgarde (kingdom)|Kingdom of Stromgarde]] wanting to annex portions of it to their kingdom while others wanted to hand the kingdom whole to an Alterac noble promising increased influence to their kingdoms.''Day of the Dragon'', pg. 6 Disagreements over what to do with the lethargic orcs (mostly pertaining to internment camp costs) created tension between some member states of the Alliance of Lordaeron.''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' Game Manual, pg. 67 The higher taxes that resulted, along with the high expense of maintaining and operating the numerous orc internment camps, led many leaders - Genn Greymane of Gilneas in particular - to believe that their kingdoms would be better off seceding from the Alliance. Quel'Thalas, led by [[Anasterian Sunstrider|King Anasterian Sunstrider]], brusquely rescinded their allegiance to the Alliance, stating that the humans' poor leadership had led to the burning of their forests during the Second War. Terenas fought back his impatience and quietly reminded the elves that nothing of Quel'Thalas would have remained if not for the hundreds of valiant humans who'd given their lives to defend it. Nonetheless, the elves stubbornly decided to go their own way. In the wake of the elves' departure, [[Gilneas (kingdom)|Gilneas]] and [[Stromgarde (kingdom)|Stromgarde]] seceded as well. However, while Admiral Proudmoore of [[Kul Tiras (kingdom)|Kul Tiras]] also briefly followed suit,[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Assault_on_Kul_Tiras_(WC2_Orc) Assault on Kul Tiras (WC2 Orc)] at some point after his nation came under attack by the [[Shadowmoon clan]] he and his nation rejoined the Alliance. In the aftermath of the splintering of the Alliance, Kul Tiras resumed its role as a stalwart ally of King Terenas along with Stormwind. Admiral Proudmoore, whose mighty fleets patrolled the trade lanes hunting pirates and marauders, maintained order on the high seas.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#A_New_Generation ''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' - A New Generation (manual text)] ===Invasion of Draenor=== Under [[Ner'zhul]]'s surgical command, the remnant orcs from [[Draenor]] eventually reassembled into the [[Horde of Draenor]], reopened the Dark Portal, raided several Alliance settlements, and rounded up several Azeroth artifacts that they needed before fleeing back to the safety of Draenor. King [[Terenas Menethil II|Terenas]] of [[Lordaeron]], convinced that the orcs were preparing a new invasion of Azeroth, assembled his most trusted lieutenants. He ordered General [[Turalyon]] and the archmage, [[Khadgar]], to lead an [[Alliance Expedition]] [[Invasion of Draenor|through the Dark Portal]] to put an end to the orcish threat once and for all. Those recruited into the Expedition included veteran heroes of the Alliance such as [[Danath Trollbane]], [[Kurdran Wildhammer]], and [[Alleria Windrunner]]. The Alliance Expedition, however, never returned because Turalyon and Khadgar agreed to make the ultimate sacrifice by destroying the Dark Portal from their side on Draenor. Though it would cost their lives, and the lives of their companions, they knew that it was the only way to ensure Azeroth's survival.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Invasion_of_Draenor] ===Third War=== Years later, an orc gladiator named [[Thrall]] led an orcish insurrection against the orcish internment camps.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_New_Horde The New Horde] Some Alliance leaders feared the young Warchief and his smaller volatile [[Horde]] may pose as dire a threat as the Old Horde did.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Warning_(WC3_Human) The Warning (WC3 Human)] At the same time, unbeknownst to the Alliance, [[Kel'Thuzad]] began forming the [[Cult of the Damned]] in Alliance lands and have been spreading the [[Plague of Undeath]] in [[Lordaeron]].[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Kel%27Thuzad_and_the_Forming_of_the_Scourge Kel'Thuzad and the Forming of the Scourge] [[Uther the Lightbringer|Uther]] and his fellow [[paladin]]s investigated the infected regions in the hope of finding a way to stop the plague. Despite their efforts, the plague continued to spread and threatened to tear the Alliance apart. As the ranks of the undead swept across Lordaeron, [[Terenas Menethil II|Terenas]]' only son, Prince [[Arthas Menethil|Arthas]], took up the fight against the [[Scourge]]. The Scourge was a difficult foe to beat, for the [[undead]] ranks swelled with every soldier that fell defending the land. Arthas began employing extreme measures to fight the undead, and his obsession with defeating the Scourge led to him losing his humanity.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Scourge_of_Lordaeron_(History_of_Warcraft) The Scourge of Lordaeron] Eventually, the Alliance was ravaged by the [[Scourge]] and the [[Burning Legion]] during the [[Third War]]. Terenas led the Alliance — since the end of the Second War — until his murder almost 15 years later at the hands of [[Arthas Menethil|Prince Arthas]], leading to the collapse of Lordaeron during the scourging of Lordaeron. Arthas attacked Quel'Thalas shortly after, ransacking the elven homeland and nearly scouring the high elves from Azeroth. The survivors of this massacre proclaimed themselves [[Blood elf|blood elves]] in honor of their peoples' fall, and a group of them joined the [[Alliance Remnants]] led by [[Othmar Garithos|Grand Marshal Garithos]] who attempted to reclaim Lordaeron from the undead. The blood elves abandoned the Alliance Remnants due to racism on behalf of its commander and left Azeroth to escape to [[Outland]]. Grand Marshal Garithos was killed in the following [[Plaguelands civil war|civil war of the Plaguelands]], and the Alliance Remnants fell apart soon after his death. ===Legacy=== Following the Third War, the balance of power among the human kingdoms shifted. With Lordaeron's fall and the devastation of the northern kingdoms, the kingdom of Stormwind arose as a new bastion of leadership and military might in the Alliance. Despite the collapse of the Alliance of Lordaeron, King Magni Bronzebeard and the dwarves of the kingdom of Ironforge remained allies of the modern Alliance,{{Alliance}} [12] [[Protecting the Herd]] becoming their staunchest and closest geographical allies. ==Organization and leadership== ===Alliance army=== * {{RaceIcon|Human|Male}} Supreme Commander [[Anduin Lothar]] ** {{RaceIcon|Human|Male}} General [[Turalyon]] ===Alliance navy=== * {{RaceIcon|Human|Male}} Grand Admiral [[Daelin Proudmoore]] ===The [[Seven Kingdoms]]=== ====[[Stormwind (kingdom)|Kingdom of Azeroth]]==== * {{RaceIcon|Human|Male}} [[Anduin Lothar]] - '''Aldrin, Protector of the Realm''' is a book that can be bought from [[Historian Samuel Ravencrest]] in [[Ravenshire]] in [[Gilneas]].

{{Book|content=
As the first crack of dawn had embraced the new realm named Gilneas, many stories and songs were made to honor the noble [[Garalon Greymane|Garalon]]. He that through fire and blood had succeeded to win the independence of the lands he was born in.
----
Although history mentions [[Aldrin Ravenwood|Aldrin]] as general of the rebel army, only whispers and myths were spread about his true character. It is believed that Aldrin was one of the unlucky children abandoned in the Ravenswood, as tribute paid to the myth known as the [[Wolf-Serpent]]. Against all odds and fate itself Aldrin managed to survive and was adopted by the Greymane nobility as the son of the cupbearer.
----
Betrayed by his own nature, Aldrin would not have been able to take over his adoptive father's task. His calling was to battle, a calling that convinced the young Greymane to employ him as his personal bodyguard. From there the two teenagers were to bond through intensive combat and strategy training as rivals. A rivalry that slowly turned into a brothership.
----
On the day that Garaleon<sup>[sic]</sup> walked the steps towards the leadership of his lands he named Aldrin his knight, and later had him become the general of the rebel army that was to defeat the Great Empire of Arathor. If Garaleon<sup>[sic]</sup> was the sword of the realm, Aldrin would be its shield. If Garaleon<sup>[sic]</sup> was the jury, Aldrin was the executioner.
----
Their friendship grew over the years, and when Garalon gave birth to the kingdom of Gilneas, Aldrin was named Lord of [[Ravenshire]] and rightful leader of [[Ravenwood Keep]]. Originally an Arathorian city-state founded after the Troll Wars, it became an independent kingdom after the empire split apart. Lastly ruled by King [[Aiden Perenolde]], Alterac was the weakest kingdom to join the [[Alliance of Lordaeron]] during the [[Second War]], and was a relatively small contributor of soldiers and supplies. As the war raged, King Perenolde lost hope of victory for humanity and betrayed his allies, forming an alliance with the Old Horde. In exchange for their protection, the orcs could pass through their lands without resistance. When the betrayal was revealed, Alterac was besieged by the Alliance and its territory was militarily occupied by Lordaeron and Stromgarde. Following the Alterac crisis, the Alteraci people are now scattered, and many of them are affiliated with the [[Syndicate]]; a criminal organization created by Lord Aliden Perenolde and led by villainous nobles of Alterac. The masks worn by the Syndicate members are orange, just like the national color of the fallen kingdom. ==History== ===Early history=== Alterac was founded as the Empire of Arathor expanded across southern Lordaeron. The early human settlers built a city nestled in the Alterac Mountains, likely exploiting its position on important trade routes through the mountains. The settlement grew into a powerful city-state around the same time as Gilneas and Kul Tiras. Originally, Gilneas and Alterac were strong supporters of Strom and had developed mighty armies that explored the mountainous southern lands of [[Khaz Modan]] and made first contact with the dwarves.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Seven_Kingdoms The Seven Kingdoms] Alterac's independence, as well as that of Kul Tiras, was won through conflict with the splintering Empire of Arathor, in which they were supported by the nascent independent nation of [[Gilneas (kingdom)|Gilneas]] and its king, [[Garalon Greymane]]. However, despite the support given to them, Alteraci assassins killed King Garalon, sparking a bloody war between the two nations that lasted several decades, ravaging the two kingdoms.[[The First Greymane]] Following the [[War of the Three Hammers]], a host of Wildhammer dwarves led by Sky King [[Morgryn]] of the fallen dwarfhold of [[Kalvanost]] made war upon the humans of [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]] and Alterac, reaping their wealth to restore his own.[[The Dwarves of Gelnor]] ===Second War=== [[File:AlteracBanner.webp|thumb|The flag of Alterac during the Second War.]] When news of the Orcish Horde arrived to Lordaeron, Alterac, led by King [[Aiden Perenolde]], was initially reluctant of joining the [[Alliance of Lordaeron]]. True to his nature of evading confrontations he did not think himself capable of winning, Perenolde sought to avoid military actions with the Horde and instead pursue diplomatic options. However, after seeing every other kingdom eventually join, and fearing being left alone to fight the Horde, Alterac finally decided to join the Alliance. However, the start of the Second War favored the orcs, and the future looked grim for the Alliance. Fearing for his kingdom should the Alliance fail, Lord Perenolde collaborated with the Orcish Horde, supplying them with information in exchange for the survival of the kingdom. Perenolde arranged for a convoy of high elves passing through Tarren Mill to be ambushed by forest trolls and organized a peasant revolt in Tyr's Hand to cover mining operations there.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Betrayal_and_the_Destruction_of_Alterac_(WC2_Human) Betrayal and the Destruction of Alterac (WC2 Human)] Alterac sailors and soldiers were eventually caught fighting for the orcs during various battles of the war.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Prisoners_(WC2_Human) The Prisoners (WC2 Human)] After Perenolde's treachery was uncovered by the Kirin Tor, the combined might of the Alliance forces, led by Dalaran mages, turned its wrath upon the small kingdom, ruthlessly crushing it as punishment for his treachery. Alterac would be put under martial law by King [[Terenas Menethil II]],''[[Day of the Dragon]]'' and Lordaeron and Stromgarde maintained garrisons along its border in the aftermath of the Second War.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Alterac_(WC2_Orc) Alterac (WC2 Orc)] ===The Alterac crisis=== When King Thoras Trollbane demanded that the eastern portion of Alterac be annexed to Stromgarde, in recognition of its efforts and sacrifices during the conflict, King Terenas Menethil II was undecided on what to do, debating the merits of either annexing Alterac to his own kingdom or setting upon its throne a new and more reasonable monarch, one that would be friendly to Lordaeron. King [[Genn Greymane]] of [[Gilneas (kingdom)|Gilneas]] also joined the dispute, supporting the claims of a nephew of Perenolde, [[Isiden Perenolde|Isiden]], who had taken refuge in Gilneas. Deathwing, disguised as Lord Daval Prestor, attempted to magically convince the leaders of the Alliance into making him Alterac's new ruler. Although he succeeded, and King Terenas planned to give control of the area to Lord Prestor, the plan was abandoned when Prestor "disappeared" (following Deathwing's defeat at Grim Batol). Isiden remained in Gilneas after the construction of the [[Greymane Wall]], and was eventually incarcerated in the Drydock Pit by [[Mortimer Harlow|Mortimer]] and [[Celia Harlow]], Alteraci nobles sent to Gilneas as envoys of Lord Prestor who acted as regents of Gilneas as King Genn Greymane's health was deteriorating. Alteraci survivors later aided Ner'zhul's forces during the shaman's quest to steal magical artifacts to open new portals. Alterac spies stole the Book of Medivh from New Stormwind, taking advantage of an assault by the forces of Shadowmoon clan led by Teron Gorefiend and the clan's Slayer.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Seas_of_Azeroth_(WC2_Orc) The Seas of Azeroth (WC2 Orc)] The Book was taken by an Alterac mage but was later given to Ner'zhul in exchange for military aid against Lordaeron and Stromgarde forces. ===Recent times=== As a kingdom, Alterac effectively ended when the forces of the Alliance overthrew Lord Perenolde, and its territories were eventually annexed by Stromgarde and Lordaeron.{{questlong|Alliance|44|Legacy of Perenolde}} At the outset of the Third War, Prince [[Arthas Menethil]] traveled through the King's Road toward Strahnbrad, and its inhabitants considered him their lord, with the citizens also taking up arms for Lordaeron.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Defense_of_Strahnbrad_(WC3_Human) The Defense of Strahnbrad (WC3 Human)] However, the Syndicate that arose during the anarchy-filled days after the nation’s dissolution became a politically active as well as militarily forceful entity. Though severed from their snowy heartland, the last of the Alteraci nobility, now leading the Syndicate, has sought to exact its revenge upon its old foe of Stromgarde. As of the current day, the old Alteraci territories continue to be disputed between the Crushridge ogres, the orcish Frostwolf clan, the dwarven Stormpike clan, and several bands of Syndicate brigands scattered across Strahnbrad and the Uplands. {{Book|content=
<The first half of the journal is entirely unremarkable. A young man's struggles with growing up supporting his family and their farm, making a living, dreams and aspirations, budding love, his favorite food, pets and horses...>

<Rather suddenly, the neat ink handwriting is replaced with a much thicker writing. Black and smudged, as though scribed with a ghostly fingertip.>
----
DAY 1

The boy was so delicious looking in his innocence. We allowed him to sleep, sleep so softly beneath my willow tree. He was warmed by the fire, though our bodies could never warm him now. We watched his nose flare with each youthful breath.

And how were we repaid? The boy knocked over the campfire to put it out. In the heat of summer, the fire spread, scorching my mushroom rings, the bark of my willow, my delicate grass blades...
----
DAY 4

We mourned, we sang songs of bereavement. It was my willow, so it is my vengeance. I followed his scent back to his farm. I observed the boy. He seemed to forget it already. I would make him remember.

At night, I so softly tapped against the window. Rapped against it. I smiled, I waved to him through the veil. Oh, the sweat of his brow! Oh, the fear in his eyes! Oh the strained beating of his heart!
----
DAY 15

He has barely slept. I always remind him I am watching. A scratching at the door, a flickering of the candles, a touch of breath against the nape of the neck, a pair of eyes in the fog. I can feel his mind growing tired, delirious, day by day.

So tired was he, he fell asleep on his feet. I allowed myself into his mind, smothered his thoughts, drowned his hopes. His body temperature dropped so deliciously. I will have to indulge myself in his dreams more and more...
----
DAY 32

His parents and friends know something is wrong. I told him not to tell. If he tells, that would make me so very upset and angry. I would be forced to extend his curse onto those he loves most. I would hate to have to do that. His parents are so very old, they would not make good dance partners. And his little love is not my type.

I ran my invisible, cold fingers through his golden mane as he returned home, today. It was barely dusk, and I had not appeared to him so early as of yet. He did not even run. He i growing accepting of his fate.
----
Day 56

He is almost gone. The boy has bags under his eyes, his hair is greying, he stutters and dares not to raise his eyes above floor level. His will is almost broken. I have begun whispering to him during the day as well as the night now. Join us... join us...

He will join us. He will join us around my willow. He will enter our circle. He will dance the black waltz. He will dance with us forever, and ever, and ever, and ever, and ever, and ever, and...

<The same words are repeated for fifty pages.>
}}

Lord '''Aldrin Ravenwood''' was a human knight and noble of the nascent [[Gilneas (kingdom)|kingdom of Gilneas]], formerly a city-state of the [[Empire of Arathor]]. A close friend to [[Garalon Greymane]], with whom he was raised as a teenager, he became the lord's bodyguard and later the general of the rebel army under Garalon's leadership during the war of Gilnean independence.

According to Gilnean legend, Aldrin was believed to be one of the unlucky children abandoned in the Ravenswood, as tribute paid to the myth known as the Wolf-Serpent. Against all odds and fate itself Aldrin managed to survive and was adopted by the Greymane nobility as the son of the cupbearer. However, Aldrin was unable to take over his adoptive father's task. His calling was to battle, a calling that convinced the young Greymane to employ him as his personal bodyguard. From there the two teenagers were to bond through intensive combat and strategy training as rivals, a rivalry that slowly turned into brotherhood.<ref name="Aldrin, Protector of the Realm">[[Aldrin, Protector of the Realm]]</ref>

On the day that Garalon started on the path to independence, he named Aldrin his knight and general of his armies. The rebel army emerged victorious against Arathor, seeing the death of [[Thoradin III]], and his son  and heir Prince [[Lenarol I]] sued for peace and bestowed upon them the lands of the Gilnean peninsula into Silverpine Forest.<ref name="TheSilverpineWars">[[The Silverpine Wars]]</ref> However, the nascent nation was soon invaded by the neighboring nation of Dalaran soon after. Gilneas emerged victorious against the Dalaranian incursion, though the nation came under threat once more when a rebellion erupted to remove King Garalon from power. As Garalon's favored general, Lord Aldrin Ravenwood had a prominent part in the subjugation of the rebellion.<ref name="TheFirstGreymane">[[The First Greymane]]</ref>

Aldin and Garalon's friendship grew over the years, and after Garalon gave birth to the kingdom of Gilneas, Aldrin was named Lord of [[Ravenshire]] and rightful leader of [[Ravenwood Keep]]. Strategically placed at the border of the lands and surrounded by the Great Sea, Aldrin would make sure that the highest and most respectable tradition would be that every Ravenwood was to be the shield of the realm until its very last man. And that the lawbreakers would have to face the fury and the loyalty of the raven that would rather cut its own wings than disrespect the word of the King.

After Garalon's death at the age of 43 by [[Alterac (kingdom)|Alteraci]] assassins, a mere few years after he had supported their secession from Arathor,<ref name="TheFirstGreymane" /> Garalon's son was mentored and regented by Lord Ravenwood after Garalon's death, ensuring that the young prince would be prepared to take the throne upon coming of age. The lasting bond between House Greymane and House Ravenwood that originated from Aldin and Garalon's friendship has endured over the following generations, as so long as a Greymane has sat upon the throne of Gilneas, a Ravenwood has stood at their side.<ref name="Aldrin, Protector of the Realm" />

Highlord '''Alexandros Mograine''', also known as the '''Ashbringer''', was the Scarlet Highlord and one of the original founders of the [[Scarlet Crusade]] along with [[High General Abbendis]] and [[Grand Inquisitor Isillien]]. ==Background== Prior to the [[Third War]], one of Mograine's sons joined the [[Alliance Expedition]] and ventured to [[Draenor]].[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Corrupted_Ashbringer/Scarlet_Monastery_Event Corrupted Ashbringer/Scarlet Monastery Event] ===The Scarlet Highlord=== Along with Abbendis and Isillien, Mograine formed the Scarlet Crusade and fought in the Third War. He would walk into whole battalions of undead and emerging unscathed - the ashes of his foes being the only indication that he had been there at all. The power of the Ashbringer came from the man who would wield it, and [[Commander Eligor Dawnbringer]] would later tell tales of the Highlord burning legions of undead in righteous fire before he would even unsheathe his blade.[[Commander Eligor Dawnbringer#Quotes]] The Highlord was the lynchpin of the Crusade. Feared by many of the Scourge, he met his end in tragedy. Through the betrayal of the Grand Crusader and Mograine's son Renault, a bargain was struck between Dathrohan and Kel'Thuzad. During a foray into the city of [[Stratholme]], Mograine was ambushed by an army of thousands of undead, and though he stood his ground, Renault made to retreat and Fairbanks was soon buried beneath a pile of Scourge corpses when he fell as his powers were exhausted. Despite their overwhelming numbers, Mograine decimated the legions of undead Scourge, and then called out for Fairbanks. However, in his moment of vulnerability, Renault picked up Ashbringer and drove it through his father's heart as his back was turned. This act of betrayal profaned the blade. However, Renault did not realize that Fairbanks had survived the ambush. For two days Fairbanks remained under the rot and contagion of Scourge, gathering as much strength as possible to escape the razed city, and much to Renault's dismay he made his way back to the [[Scarlet Monastery]]. There he told the tale of the Highlord's death to any that would listen, though he would be murdered in cold blood for his actions and dragged to a hidden chamber within the cathedral. Though manipulated into attempting to retrieve the blade in his grief, Renault was unsuccessful. Despite his controversial death, Mograine remained a martyr to the knights and warriors of Lordaeron, who would wear similarly fashioned suits in honor of their fallen hero.[[Korfax, Champion of the Light#Quotes]] As one of the Four Horsemen, he fought the heroes of the Argent Dawn when they entered [[Naxxramas]]. The [[Corrupted Ashbringer]] was reclaimed from Naxxramas, and on the urging of Mograine's spirit within, it was brought to the Scarlet Monastery. Though Renault welcomed the bearer of the Corrupted Ashbringer and granted him or her command of his forces, Mograine's spirit manifested to confront his son. Renault begged his father for forgiveness and is quickly struck down by him, saying that he is forgiven. Archbishop '''Alonsus Faol''' was the head of the [[Church of Light]] and abbot of the [[Brotherhood of Northshire|Holy Order of Northshire Clerics]] prior to the [[First War]] between humans and orcs. 

==Biography==
Prior to the [[First War]], on his fourteenth birthday [[Medivh]] fell into coma and the Abbot and the [[Barathen Wrynn|King]] agreed that the future Guardian be taken into [[Northshire Abbey]].<ref>''Warcraft: Orcs & Humans'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft:_Orcs_%26_Humans_manual#571 Chronicles of the War in Azeroth]'', 571</ref> During the course of the war, the Abbot received a vision about Sir [[Anduin Lothar]] being trapped in the [[Deadmines]] so [[Llane Wrynn I|King Llane]] sent the [[Defender of the Crown]] to rescue the missing knight.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Dead_Mines_(WC1_Human) The Dead Mines (WC1 Human)]</ref>

Following the terrible attrition suffered by his clerics in that conflict and the destruction of [[Northshire Abbey]], the aged Faol fled with the surviving citizens of [[Stormwind (kingdom)|Stormwind]] to [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]]. Aided by his apprentice, [[Uther the Lightbringer|Uther Lightbringer]], Faol founded the [[Order of the Knights of the Silver Hand]], this time equipping the followers of the Holy Light in the armaments of war.<ref>''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#Alliance_Ground_Units Alliance Ground Units]'', Paladin</ref> [[Alonsus Chapel]], in Stratholme, was the site where he anointed Uther as the first of the paladins.<ref>[[Aurius#Quotes]]</ref>

Following the [[Second War]], Archbishop Alonsus Faol worked ceaselessly to rebuild the [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Kingdom of Lordaeron]] and bring aid to the remaining nations of the [[Alliance of Lordaeron]].<ref>''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos Game Manual''</ref> He helped to reform the [[Brotherhood of Northshire]] and raised vast funds to rebuild [[Stormwind City]].<ref>[[Alonsus Faol#Death and remembrance]]</ref> He also took under his wing the kindly [[Archbishop Benedictus|Benedictus]] and spent many years teaching him the ways of the [[Light]], and together, they built the [[Cathedral of Light]] in [[Stormwind City]].<ref name="WoW Manual">''World of Warcraft: Game Manual'', pg. 170</ref>

During the trial of [[Tirion Fordring]] in [[Stratholme]], he held the position of one of the four jurors. Like the other judges, he was shocked when Tirion admitted his guilt, for taking a vow of honor to protect the orc [[Eitrigg]] and refusing to break it, which led the paladin to his excommunication and his exile.<ref>''[[Of Blood and Honor]]'', chapter 5</ref>

==Death and remembrance==
Alonsus Faol died at some point prior to the [[Third War]] and was succeeded as Archbishop by his apprentice [[Archbishop Benedictus|Benedictus]], who swore to continue the good work his mentor had begun so many years ago.<ref name="WoW Manual"/> He is presumed to have been buried at [[Faol's Rest]], a graveyard in the now-plagued Tirisfal Glades, located near the Scarlet Monastery.

A statue and fountain stands in front of the [[Cathedral of Light]] in [[Stormwind City]], honoring all the hard work done by Faol during the First and Second Wars, notably his raising funds to help rebuild the city and to reestablish the Brotherhood of Northshire.

Long ago, before the [[First War]], the [[warlock]] [[Gul'dan]] exiled a clan of [[orc]]s called the [[Frostwolves]] to a hidden valley deep in the heart of the [[Alterac Mountains]]. It is here in the valley's southern reaches that the Frostwolves eked out a living until the coming of [[Thrall]].

After Thrall's triumphant uniting of the clans, the Frostwolves, now led by the Orc [[Shaman]] [[Drek'Thar]], chose to remain in the valley they had for so long called their home. In recent times, however, the relative peace of the Frostwolves has been challenged by the arrival of the [[Dwarven]] [[Stormpike Expedition]].

The Stormpikes have set up residence in the valley to search for natural resources and ancient relics. Despite their intentions, the Dwarven presence has sparked heated conflict with the Frostwolf Orcs to the south, who have vowed to drive the interlopers from their lands. 

= Overview =
In Alterac Valley, your goal is to push your way to the other faction's base, and kill the enemy General. Along the way, you have to deal with Bunkers, Towers, and tons of [[NPC]]s. There can be up to 40 players on each side, and the minimum level requirement is 51. The game usually lasts hours.

The official Alliance entrance is in The Headlands north of [[Southshore]]. However like all [[BG]]s you can enter through a [[Battlemaster]]. Once inside the instance, the alliance base rests in the north. Their primary fortress is called [[Alterac Valley#Dun Balder|Dun Balder]] in which resides their [[Alterac Valley#Generals|General]]; [[Vanndar Stormpike]]. The Alliance [[Alterac Valley#Captains|Captain]] is [[Balinda Stonehearth]] who stays in [[Alterac Valley#Stonehearth Outpost|Stonehearth Outpost]]. There are 4 Alliance [[Alterac Valley#Commanders|Commanders]] and 6 Alliance [[Alterac Valley#Lieutenants|Lieutenants]] scattered throughout the [[Alterac Valley#Towers|Towers]] and [[Alterac Valley#Graveyards|Graveyards]].

*'''Horde Entrance:''' North of [[Tarren Mill]]

==Generals==
The objective of Alterac Valley is to slay the opposing General. Killing the General ends the game. The Alliance General is [[Vanndar Stormpike]]. He is located in [[Alterac Valley#Dun Balder|Dun Balder]]. The Horde General is [[Drek'thar]]. He is located in [[Alterac Valley#Frostwolf Keep|Frostwolf Keep]]. Generals must be killed inside their keep. If they are [[kite]]d outside they will [[leash]] back inside.

==Captains==
There are 2 Captains in Alterac Valley, one for each side. The Captains periodically buff all [[PC]] allies in Alterac Valley a size, DPS and HP buff. If your captain dies, this periodic buff is disabled, and troops that normally spawn around the Captain cease to spawn. Also, the opposing side will receive more buffs providing their Captain is still alive.

The Alliance Captain is [[Balinda Stonehearth]] who resides in [[Alterac Valley#Stone Hearth Outpost|Stonehearth Outpost]]). The Horde Captain is [[Galvanger]] who resides in [[Alterac Valley#Iceblood Garrison|Iceblood Garrison]].

= Buildings in Alterac Valley =
== Bunkers and Towers ==
Bunkers are Alliance defensive structures, and Towers are Horde defensive structures. Each side has 4 of these buildings, and 3 house an enemy [[Alterac Valley#Wing Commander Quests|Wing Commander]]. 2 of the 4 house a [[Alterac Valley#Commanders|Commander]]. These towers have ranged attackers posted inside them that shoot enemies outside the structure. Towers and Bunkers can be destroyed if an enemy player captures the [[flag]] inside. This will prevent the ranged fighters from attacking and allows an opportunity to save your [[Alterac Valley#Wing Commander Quests|Wing Commander]].

== Graveyards ==
Graveyards are where dead [[PC]]s ressurect upon death. If you die in Alterac Valley you will resurrect at the closest graveyard that your side controls. Capturing graveyards is therefore a critical part in the Alterac Valley assault because it allows [[PC]] reinforcements to arrive much more speedily.

By capturing a graveyard you change the resurrection location to that new graveyard. When a graveyard is under control, it is protected by troop as well as a lieutenant to prevent capturing. There are 7 Graveyards in total. Details on tlocs and NPC involvement to follow.

= Reputation =
As you fight in Alterac Valley, you earn reputation with either the [[Frostwolf Clan]] for [[Horde]] or the [[Stormpike Guard]] for [[Alliance]]. Higher ranks with your respective faction will allow you to purchase items from your faction's vendor. There are two vendors for each faction; one inside Alterac Valley and one outside in [[Hillsbrad Foothills]]. [http://www.worldofwarcraft.com/ Worldofwarcraft.com] has a complete list of [http://worldofwarcraft.com/pvp/battlegrounds/rewards-alterac.html Alterac Valley vendor rewards].

Note that in Alterac Valley all reputation with Stormpike/Frostwolves is shared amoungst all combatants, whether or not they are partied with you or not. However some turns in will give reputation with one of the 4 main primary factions. This faction is not shared.

'''Stormpike/Frostwolf reputation is gained in the following ways:'''
* Killing the enemy General (300 rep)
* Killing the enemy Captain (125 rep)
* Killing an enemy Lieutenant or Commander (12 rep)
* Killing an enemy Wind Rider (5 rep)
* Killing any Enemy Guard (5 rep) *NOTE: Might be capped through honored like Argent Dawn, doesn't give rep in exalted*
* Killing [[Ivus the Forest Lord]] or [[Lok'holar]] (125 rep)
* Destroying an enemy tower (12 rep)
* 1-time quests (first turnin of each repeatable, capture a tower/mine/graveyard, etc) (~100 rep each, varies)
* '''Repeatable turnin quests'''
** Supplies from enemy's mine (10 rep)
** Supplies from your mine (2 rep)
** Racial parts (Human bone chip, Tauren hoof, etc) (1 rep) This also yields 10 faction with one of the 4 primary factions.
** Ram hide/frostwolf hide (2 rep)
** Bringing a ram/frostwolf to your stable (1 rep)
** Storm Crystals/Stormpike Blood (1 rep, 5 rep for Crystal Cluster or Gallon of Blood)
** '''Wind Riders'''
*** Sildore/Guse (1 rep)
*** Vipore/Jeztor (2 rep)
*** Ichman/Mulverik (5 rep)
* '''At the end of the game, extra rep is gained for each of the following conditions:'''
** Enemy Captain killed (36 rep)
** Your Captain is still alive (125 rep)
** Enemy tower destroyed (24 rep each)
** Enemy Leutenant/Commander killed (12 rep each)
** Controlling an intact tower (12 rep each)
** Controlling a graveyard (12 rep each)
** Controlling a mine (12 rep each)

'''Ambermill''' is a human village located slightly southwest of Lordamere Lake. It is occupied by forces of the [[Kirin Tor]], who are still considered to be part of the [[Alliance]]. 

Prior to the advent of the [[Third War]], Ambermill was a relatively unimportant site in western [[Dalaran]], but following the rampage of the [[Scourge]] and [[Burning Legion]] through the northlands, the rebuilding wizards of Dalaran began to form plans for the strategic use of the hamlet. Ambermill was located atop a dormant ley energy node, and in order to combat the [[Forsaken]] and other menaces, the Kirin Tor has attempted to reactivate the node. 

Ambermill provides a safe haven for those Alliance adventurers traveling to the [[Tirisfal Glades]] and beyond. However, Ambermill is not the safest Alliance haven, and nor does it have many Alliance-friendly vendors.

The '''Alterac crisis''',<ref>''[[Day of the Dragon]]'', pg. 5</ref> also referred to as the '''Alterac Succession Crisis''',<ref name="The Greymane Stone">{{questlong|Horde|47D|The Greymane Stone}}</ref> was a political dispute between the nations of [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]], [[Gilneas (kingdom)|Gilneas]], [[Kul Tiras (kingdom)|Kul Tiras]], and [[Stromgarde (kingdom)|Stromgarde]] on what should happen to the traitorous nation of [[Alterac (kingdom)|Alterac]] and its lands in the aftermath of the [[Second War]]. The dispute at points threatened to tear the [[Alliance of Lordaeron|Alliance]] apart, and the [[black dragon]] [[Deathwing]] unsuccessfully tried to use the crisis to his advantage to take control of Alterac.

==History==
===Background===
[[Aiden Perenolde]], King of Alterac, had come to believe that only the surrender of his forces and his sovereignty would save the lives of his subjects, and thus betrayed the Alliance to the [[Orcish Horde]] in exchange for the safety of Alterac.<ref>''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#Alterac Nations of the Alliance]'', Alterac</ref> To this end, he arranged for a peasant revolt in [[Tyr's Hand]] to cover Horde mining operations there, kidnapped mages from [[Dalaran (kingdom)|Dalaran]] and arranged for a convoy of high elves passing through Tarren Mill to be ambushed by forest trolls.<ref name="BetrayalAndDestruction">[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Betrayal_and_the_Destruction_of_Alterac_(WC2_Human) Betrayal and the Destruction of Alterac (WC2 Human)]</ref> When Lord Perenolde's treachery was discovered by the Kirin Tor, the combined might of the Alliance forces, led by Dalaran mages, turned its wrath upon the small kingdom, ruthlessly crushing it as punishment for his treachery<ref name="BetrayalAndDestruction" /> and establishing martial law under Lordaeron's forces.<ref name="DotD">''[[Day of the Dragon]]''</ref>

===Day of the Dragon===
In the aftermath of the Second War, the nations of Lordaeron and Stromgarde maintained garrisons along Alterac's borders.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Alterac_(WC2_Orc) Alterac (WC2 Orc)]</ref> King [[Thoras Trollbane]], in recognition of Stromgarde's efforts and sacrifices during the conflict, demanded that the eastern portion of Alterac be annexed to Stromgarde. However, King Terenas Menethil II was undecided on what to do, debating the merits of either annexing Alterac to his own kingdom or setting upon its throne a new and more reasonable monarch, one that would be friendly to Lordaeron.<ref name="DotD" /> Lord Perenolde's precarious situation saw his nephew [[Isiden Perenolde|Isiden]] seeking refuge in Gilneas, where his quest for backing led him to the attention of King [[Genn Greymane]] as the delicate issue of Alteraci succession gained momentum.<ref name="Legacy of Perenolde">{{questlong|Alliance|44|Legacy of Perenolde}}</ref> King Greymane's support of Isiden Perenolde drew the ire of [[Daelin Proudmoore|Admiral Proudmoore]], who was afraid that Gilnean influence in the region would threaten Kul Tiras' naval sovereignty.<ref>''[[Day of the Dragon]]'', chapter 1</ref>

The black dragon [[Deathwing]], under the guise of Lord Daval Prestor, manipulated the leaders into making him the future king of Alterac. This worked for a time, but drew the suspicious attention of the [[Kirin Tor]] of [[Dalaran (kingdom)|Dalaran]], who were conveniently left out of the negotiations by the black dragon. During the crisis, Lord Prestor often frequented [[Gilneas City]] and established a close bond with King Greymane, bestowing upon him a gift: a potent artifact known as the [[Shard of Midnight]].<ref name="The Greymane Stone" /> Two Alteraci nobles, Lord [[Mortimer Harlow|Mortimer]] and Lady [[Celia Harlow]], were also sent to Gilneas as envoys of Lord Prestor.

Prestor tried to have the Kirin Tor ostracized by the other Alliance leaders and even secured a betrothal to Lordaeron's princess, [[Calia Menethil|Calia]], in order to reinforce his political position. Ultimately, however, Deathwing's plans were foiled when he was defeated at the [[Battle of Grim Batol]] and forced into hiding.<ref name="DotD" />

===Resolution===
With Deathwing's disappearance, his magical influence on the human kings waned away. [[Genn Greymane]] reinstated his protest against Daval Prestor's taking ascension, and even Lord Admiral Proudmoore joined him on this. King Terenas announced that a second check into the so-called noble's background left many questions unanswered, and the wedding was canceled.<ref>''[[Day of the Dragon]]'', chapter 21</ref>

As a kingdom, Alterac effectively ended when the forces of the Alliance overthrew Lord Perenolde, and its territories were eventually annexed by Stromgarde and Lordaeron.<ref name="Legacy of Perenolde" /> At the outset of the [[Third War]], [[Arthas Menethil]] traveled through the [[King's Road]] toward [[Strahnbrad]], and its inhabitants considered him their lord, with the citizens also taking up arms for Lordaeron.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Defense_of_Strahnbrad_(WC3_Human) The Defense of Strahnbrad (WC3 Human)]</ref> A new resistance against them had appeared, however, in the form of the [[Syndicate]], led by former Alteraci prince [[Aliden Perenolde]] under the teachings of his mentor [[Aedelas Blackmoore]].<ref>{{questlong|Horde|36|Blackmoore's Legacy}}</ref> Isiden remained in Gilneas even after the closure of the [[Greymane Wall]], and was eventually incarcerated in the [[Dryrock Pit]] by the Harlows, who had begun acting as regents of Gilneas as King Genn Greymane's health was deteriorating.
